title_en: Great Poems and Songs (13/20): Xin Qiji, the Poet with a Sword
note_en: Chinese has two particles both pronounced de that English handles with "'s" and "-ly": 的 links a description to a noun (他的词 "his poems," 家乡的义军 "a volunteer army from his hometown"), while 地 turns a description into an adverb before a verb (勇敢地和敌人打仗 "fought the enemy bravely"). The sound is the same; the character and its position tell you which job de is doing.

sentences.en: This poem has a surprising ending: "To finish my sovereign's great task of reuniting the realm, and win a name in life and after death—alas, my hair has already turned white!" One moment he is picturing victory and great deeds; the last line suddenly turns into "what a pity my hair is already white," and this sharp drop in mood is what moves readers most.
